sources.entry: micropython - A lean and efficient Python implementation for microcontrollers and constrained systems.

summary.one_liner: MicroPython is a lean implementation of Python 3 for microcontrollers, embedded systems, and other constrained platforms, with a core VM plus many hardware ports.
summary.what_it_does: The repository contains the core Python implementation (compiler, runtime, core library) written in C, plus the mpy-cross cross-compiler that turns scripts into precompiled .mpy bytecode. It supports a large part of Python 3 syntax and core types (str, bytes, list, dict, set, namedtuple, classes, and more), and builtin modules such as os, sys, time, re, and struct, with some ports offering _thread, socket, ssl, and asyncio. It also provides MicroPython-specific modules for hardware access such as GPIO, timers, ADC, DAC, PWM, SPI, I2C, CAN, Bluetooth, and USB. The ports/ directory holds platform-specific code for many targets, grouped into three support tiers, and the Unix and Windows ports can be used for development and testing. Scripts can run from source or bytecode, from an on-device filesystem or frozen into the firmware.
use_cases: programming ESP32 or Raspberry Pi Pico boards in Python
running Python on microcontrollers with limited flash and RAM
controlling GPIO, PWM, SPI, I2C hardware from Python
lightweight Python interpreter on embedded Linux
porting a Python runtime to a new microcontroller
how_to_run: Build the chosen port with make (gmake on BSD-based systems); requires bash, gcc, and python3
Some ports (rp2, esp32) additionally require CMake
notable: Runs on dozens of ports, from tiny Cortex-M and ESP32 boards to Linux, macOS, and Windows
Includes mpy-cross to precompile scripts into frozen .mpy bytecode
Tiered port support model (Tier 1, 2, 3) indicating maturity
Designed for Python compatibility so most scripts run unchanged
Includes a minimal port intended as a starting template for new microcontroller ports
caveats: Only a subset of Python 3 functionality is implemented for data types and modules
Lower-tier and Tier 3 ports are less actively tested; some ports are maintenance-only
Smallest targets need roughly 256kiB flash and 16kiB RAM, and fuller features need more
